title: Etale local splitting of a cover over a finite scheme
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:Z\to U$ be a finite morphism of $S$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $W$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and let $q:W\to Z$ be representable, surjective and etale [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then there exist an $S$-scheme $U'$, a surjective etale morphism $v:U'\to U$, and a morphism
$$\sigma:Z\times_UU'\longrightarrow W\times_UU'$$
which is a section of $q_{U'}:W\times_UU'\to Z\times_UU'$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Neither flatness of $p$ nor separatedness or quasi-compactness of $q$ is assumed. Empty schemes are allowed.

proof.text: Representability of $q$ makes $W$ a scheme: test the definition on $Z\to Z$, so $W=W\times_ZZ$ is represented. Fix $u\in U$ and restrict to an affine open neighbourhood $U_0$ of $u$. The base-changed $Z_0$ is finite over $U_0$, hence affine, and its fibre over $u$ is a finite set $\{z_1,\ldots,z_r\}$. Choose $w_i\in W$ over $z_i$ and an affine open neighbourhood $A_i$ of $w_i$ in $W\times_UU_0$. Put $A=\coprod_iA_i$ and $H=Z_0\amalg A$, with the induced maps to $U_0$. These are finite coproducts of affines, hence affine. The map $a:A\to Z_0$ restricts on each summand to $q$ composed with an open immersion, so is etale, as is checked on those open summands. If $r=0$, the closed-image property of $p$ gives the neighbourhood $U_0\setminus p(Z_0)$ of $u$ on which $Z$ is empty; the unique empty-domain map is already a section there. Hence assume $r>0$.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, reduction to schemes and choice of the finitely many points; use affine neighbourhoods of the chosen lifts instead of an entire separated atlas

proof.text: The finite ring map defining $Z_0\to U_0$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime, so this map is locally quasi-finite. Since $a$ is etale, it is unramified, and the unramified quasi-finiteness theorem makes $a$ locally quasi-finite. Composition makes $A\to U_0$ locally quasi-finite. Therefore $H\to U_0$ is locally quasi-finite, checked on its open summands, and is locally of finite type. Every chosen $z_i$ and $w_i$ is isolated in the fibre: in an affine neighbourhood in the definition of local quasi-finiteness its fibre singleton is open, hence also open in the entire fibre. Finally $H\to U_0$ is separated because $H$ is affine. Thus the isolated-point splitting theorem applies to $H\to U_0$ and the pairwise distinct list consisting of all the $z_i$ and the marked $w_i$ in their separate summands.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, application of the separated locally-finite-type isolated-point splitting lemma: verification of its hypotheses

proof.text:
Apply the isolated-point splitting theorem once to this list in $H$. It gives an etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(U_0,u)$ and finitely many clopen pieces finite over $T$, each with singleton fibre over $t$ and finite purely inseparable residue extension over $\kappa(t)$; the remaining clopen has no point above any marked point. Intersect the pieces with the original clopen summands $Z_0$ and $A_i$. These intersections are still clopen and finite: locally a clopen subscheme of a finite $R$-algebra $C$ has ring $C/I$, a quotient of the finite $R$-module $C$. The intersections retaining the marked fibre points give
$$Z_T=D\amalg\coprod_{j\in J}V_j,$$
where $J$ is finite, $(V_j)_t=\{z_j'\}$ and $D_t=\varnothing$, and give clopen finite pieces $B_l\subseteq A_T$ with $(B_l)_t=\{b_l\}$ over the original marked $w_i$. Their residue fields are finite purely inseparable over $\kappa(t)$. Every point of $(A_i)_T$ over $t$ mapping to its marked $w_i$ lies in one of these $B_l$. The map $D\to T$ is finite by the same quotient argument, since $Z_T\to T$ is finite. Delete its closed image, which misses $t$. Replace $T$ by that open neighbourhood, so $D=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, simultaneous isolated-point decomposition and deletion of the unused finite component

proof.text:
For each $j$, the point $z_j'$ maps to some original $z_i$. There is a point of $(A_i)_T$ above $z_j'$ and mapping to the original $w_i$: apply the fibre-product point description to $A_i\to Z_0$ and $Z_T\to Z_0$. The relevant ring is
$$\kappa(z_j')\otimes_{\kappa(z_i)}\kappa(w_i).$$
The field-extension faithfully-flat lemma and surjectivity on spectra give a prime of this ring (start with the zero prime of $\kappa(z_j')$). This point lies over $t$, hence lies in a piece $B_{l(j)}$ by the exhaustion clause of step 3. Its singleton fibre point $b_{l(j)}$ therefore maps to $z_j'$. Choices for different $j$ need not use distinct $B_l$; their restrictions to the disjoint $V_j$ below suffice.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, choice of a matching finite piece above each point of the split finite scheme

proof.text: Set $C_j=B_{l(j)}\cap a_T^{-1}(V_j)$. This is a clopen subscheme of $B_{l(j)}$, contains $b_{l(j)}$, and is finite over $T$ by the quotient-of-a-finite-module argument of step 3. The morphism $f_j:C_j\to V_j$ is finite by finite permanence over a separated target, since both schemes are finite over $T$. It is etale: $\{a:A\to Z_0,\mathrm{id}_{Z_0}\}$ is a jointly surjective etale family, so the covering-base-change theorem makes $a_T$ etale, and the restriction to the open source $C_j$ and open target $V_j$ preserves etaleness. Its fibre over $z_j'$ is exactly $\{b_{l(j)}\}$, since every such point lies over $t$. The residue extension $\kappa(b_{l(j)})/\kappa(z_j')$ is purely inseparable. Indeed both fields contain $\kappa(t)$ compatibly and every element of the larger field has a $p$-power in $\kappa(t)\subseteq\kappa(z_j')$ in characteristic $p$; in characteristic zero both equal $\kappa(t)$.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, finite etale maps between matching pieces and their singleton purely inseparable fibres

proof.text:
Apply the finite-unramified singleton-fibre theorem to $f_j$ at $z_j'$: finiteness, uniqueness of the fibre point and the purely inseparable residue extension were proved in step 5, and etaleness supplies unramifiedness. It gives an open neighbourhood $O_j$ of $z_j'$ on which $f_j$ is a closed immersion. This restricted morphism is still etale: restrict the source by an open immersion, compose with $f_j$, then cancel the open immersion of its target using etale composition and cancellation. The etale closed-immersion theorem makes it an open immersion and an isomorphism onto its open image, which contains $z_j'$. Shrink $O_j$ to that image. Thus
$$f_j^{-1}(O_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}O_j.$$
This is the singleton finite-etale argument used in the source, assembled from the two existing nodes rather than introduced as another lemma.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, the singleton finite-etale fibre gives an isomorphism on a neighbourhood

proof.text:
For each $j$, $V_j\setminus O_j$ is closed in $V_j$ and its image under the finite map $V_j\to T$ is closed. None of these images contains $t$, since $(V_j)_t=\{z_j'\}\subseteq O_j$. Delete their finite union from $T$. On the resulting open neighbourhood $N$ of $t$, every $(V_j)_N$ lies in $O_j$, so
$$(C_j)_N\xrightarrow{\sim}(V_j)_N.$$
Its inverse followed by $(C_j)_N\to A_N\to W_N$ is a section over $(V_j)_N$. The clopen pieces $(V_j)_N$ are pairwise disjoint and exhaust $Z_N$ by step 3; the coproduct mapping property therefore combines these morphisms into $\sigma_N:Z_N\to W_N$. On every summand $q_N\sigma_N$ is the identity, hence it is the identity on $Z_N$. The morphism $N\to U$ is etale, being the composite of open immersions and $T\to U_0$.

source.place: Tag 05XQ, lemma-surjection-space-of-sections, shrinking away the bad closed images and assembling the inverse maps

proof.text: Perform this construction for every $u\in U$, choosing one neighbourhood $N_u\to U$ with a point over $u$, and put $U'=\coprod_{u\in U}N_u$. The induced map $v:U'\to U$ is surjective because each $u$ has its selected lift. It is etale since on each open summand it is the etale map $N_u\to U$, and etaleness is defined locally on source and target. Pulling back the open-and-closed summands of $U'$ gives the disjoint open covering $Z\times_UU'=\coprod_u Z_{N_u}$: this follows directly from the fibre-product universal property, or by restricting to each summand. The maps $\sigma_{N_u}$ combine by the coproduct mapping property to $\sigma:Z\times_UU'\to W\times_UU'$, with $q_{U'}\sigma=\mathrm{id}$ checked on the summands. All structure maps are over $U$, hence over $S$. The index set and the coproduct are in the stated universes. If $U$ is empty use the empty coproduct; if $Z$ is empty use $U'=U$ and the unique map from the empty scheme.

Steps checked against the cited statements. Step 1: W is a scheme by representability, Z_0 is affine (finite permanence (b)), the fibre is finite, a|A_i is q composed with an open immersion, and r=0 is handled by the closed image. Step 2: all hypotheses of 02LO (lem-sfb-etale-splits-isolated-purely-inseparable) hold for H=Z_0⊔A: locally quasi-finite through the finite ring map, unramified and composition; locally of finite type; separated because H is affine; the marked points are distinct because they lie in distinct summands. Step 3: clopen pieces are Spec(Ce), so finite. D_t=∅ because every fibre point of Z_0 over u is marked (the text leaves this implicit), and the exhaustion of the B_l is correct. Step 4: (A_i)_T=A_i×_{Z_0}Z_T, and a nonempty tensor of residue fields gives the lift through faithful flatness and surjectivity on spectra. Step 5: f_j is finite by 035D and étale as the base change of a, using the {a,id} covering trick; the fibre is a singleton, and κ(b)/κ(z_j') is purely inseparable because it sits between fields over κ(t). Step 6: 04DG and then the étale closed immersion lemma replace the source's 04DH argument validly. Steps 7–8: shrinking by finite closed images, coproduct assembly and the empty cases are correct.
